newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso pares slide at close on auction hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso pares slide at close on auction hopes.

text.p: The Mexican peso pared earlier losses against the dollar at the close of trade on Monday on market predictions of impending increases in primary interest rates, traders said.
"The peso firmed up at the close, I saw dollars flowing into Mexico," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 1.4 and 1.5 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.9100/7.9140 and 7.9070/7.9110 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts earlier closed 3.3 centavos weaker at 7.9210/7.9260 per dollar.
The 48-hour peso had opened 3.5 centavos weaker at 7.9280/7.9140 per dollar.
"Some local dealers bought dollars this morning, thinking the peso would slide further, but sold them off towards the close," another trader said.

Money market traders forecast an increase of up to 60 basis points on bellwether 28-day Cetes rates, which currently stand at 20.59 percent, at Tuesday evening's central bank auction of government securities.
"Cetes rates may rise a little due to U.S. long bond yields," a peso dealer meanwhile said.
Yields on the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond stood at 7.10 percent, up from 7.00 percent last Wednesday.
Mexican financial markets were closed on Thursday, March 27, when U.S. long bond yields increased sharply.
